glossary.definition: (i) "Office equipment" includes but is not limited to typewriters, copying and duplicating equipment, and computer and data processing equipment.

glossary.definition:
(ii) "Software for instructional purposes" includes computer programs usable for computer assisted instruction, computer managed instruction, drill and practice, and problem simulations.

(b) A board of education or governing board of an educational service center may acquire the necessary office equipment, and computer hardware and software for instructional purposes, for the schools under its control by purchase, by lease, by installment payments, by entering into lease-purchase agreements, or by lease with an option to purchase. In the case of a city, exempted village, or local school district, if the purchase price is to be paid over a period of time, the contract setting forth the terms of such purchase shall be considered a continuing contract pursuant to section 5705.41 of the Revised Code. Payments shall not extend for a period of more than five years. Costs relating to the acquisition of necessary apparatus may be paid from funds available to the school district or educational service center for operating purposes.

(c) In acquiring technological equipment and computer hardware and software under division (B)(4)(b) of this section, the board of education or governing board shall seek to meet the varying and unique needs of students and teachers in the schools under its control, and shall consider all of the following:

(i) The long-term cost of ownership;

(ii) Flexibility for innovation;

(iii) Any anticipated residual or salvage value at the end of the target life cycle.

(5) A board of education or governing board of an educational service center may acquire the necessary equipment for the maintenance or physical upkeep of facilities and land under its control by entering into lease-purchase agreements. If payments under the lease-purchase agreement are to be made over a period of time, the agreement shall be considered a continuing contract pursuant to section 5705.41 of the Revised Code, and such payments shall not extend for a period of more than five years.
